newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues sees no telecom profit until 2001.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues sees no telecom profit until 2001.

text.p: French building group Bouygues does not expect Bouygues Telecoms to make a positive contribution to the group's results until the year 2001, chairman Martin Bouygues said on Monday.

He told a news conference the telecoms unit's contribution to group results would be a deficit of 340 million francs ($58.3 million) this year, a deficit of 290 million in 1998, and deficits of 185 million for the years 1999 and 2000. In 2001 it is expected to make a positive contribution of 350 million francs.
Bouygues Telecoms' results had a negative impact last year of 144 million francs on turnover of 236 million.
Sales are expected to rise sharply to 950 million francs this year, 2.5 billion in 1998, five billion in 1999, eight billion in 2000 and 10.9 billion in 2001.
Bouygues' market share is expected to rise to eight percent this year from four percent in 1996 and grow steadily to reach 22 percent in 2000 or 2001, he said.

Bouygues and its Italian partner STET were collaborating in seeking out niche opportunities. "Bouygues wants to develop its telecoms activities and, along with our partner, study different market segments...That will determine our strategies and the alliances we need to build," he said.
Bouygues said the group's financial structure and "abundant cash" would enable it to make the investments necessary for its development.

Bouygues Telecom holds the group's telecommunications interests, including one of France's two private sector franchises for mobile telephones, and rivals the larger Cegetel subsidiary of Cie Generale des Eaux.
